purpose: Authoritative application of harvest/authors/github-match-audit.json. This file is the decision record; harvest/authors/apply_link_overrides.py folds it into links.json. Written by the coordinator on his instruction, 2026-08-26.
rule_drop: Remove EVERY candidate whose source begins with 'github_' (github_profile, github_blog, github_email) for the people listed in 'drop'. The blog and email were read off the wrong person's GitHub profile, so they are wrong for the same reason the handle is — 31 candidates across 17 people, not 17.
rule_hold: Keep the candidate in the data but set publish:false. It may not be rendered as anyone's link until a second signal exists: the handle appears as a contributor on the paper's own repo, or on the person's homepage or LinkedIn.
rule_never_primary: Accounts with zero public repositories stay, but must never be a person's primary/rendered link. Prefer any other tier.
rule_human_supplied: Links he supplied directly, 2026-08-26, for people the audit left linkless or wrongly linked. These are authoritative: inserted as the FIRST candidate, source 'human', outranking anything harvested. Tier follows the link ruling — a faculty/institutional page is permanent-academic, otherwise linkedin.
rule_suppress: Candidates he has explicitly ruled against. Set publish:false so the renderer skips them even though the tier would otherwise win.
status: Applied and pushed 2026-08-26: drops (upstream worker), 19 held, 20 never-primary, 13 human links, 1 suppression. Rerun is a no-op.
